```{r libraries, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, 
  warning = FALSE, 
  message = FALSE)
library(data.table)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ape)
library(phytools)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(Cairo)
library(phylocanvas)
options(bitmapType = 'cairo')
```

```{r import_files, include=FALSE}
samples <- fread(linkages) %>% rename(sample_id = sample)

#----- CORE SNP TREE WRANGLING ------# 

## Read tree and extract tip order
snp_tree <- read.tree(snptree)
snp_tree <- midpoint_root(snp_tree)
snp_tree <- ladderize(snp_tree, right = F) 
snp_tree_tip_order <- snp_tree$tip.label

#------------ GUBBINS TREE ----------------------#
gub_tree <- read.tree(gubtree)
gub_tree <- midpoint_root(gub_tree)
gub_tree <- ladderize(gub_tree, right = F) 

#------------ MASH TREE ----------------------#
mash_tree <- read.tree(mashtree)
if (!is.null(mash_tree$edge.length) && sum(mash_tree$edge.length) > 0) {
  mash_tree <- midpoint_root(mash_tree)
}
mash_tree <- ladderize(mash_tree, right = F) 

#----- DISTANCE MATRICES WRANGLING ------# 
# Read and reorder SNP distance matrix
snp_df <- fread(snpmatrix, data.table = FALSE) 
row_names <- snp_df[[1]]
snp_matrix <- as.matrix(snp_df[, -1])
rownames(snp_matrix) <- row_names
colnames(snp_matrix) <- row_names
snp_matrix <- snp_matrix[snp_tree_tip_order, snp_tree_tip_order]
snp_matrix[upper.tri(snp_matrix)] <- NA

# Read and reorder Gubbins SNP distance matrix
gub_snp_df <- fread(gubmatrix, data.table = FALSE) 
row_names <- gub_snp_df[[1]]
gub_snp_matrix <- as.matrix(gub_snp_df[, -1])
rownames(gub_snp_matrix) <- row_names
colnames(gub_snp_matrix) <- row_names
gub_snp_matrix <- gub_snp_matrix[snp_tree_tip_order, snp_tree_tip_order]
gub_snp_matrix[upper.tri(gub_snp_matrix)] <- NA

# Read and reorder Mash distance matrix
mash_df <- fread(mashmatrix, data.table = FALSE) 
row_names <- mash_df[[1]]
mash_matrix <- as.matrix(mash_df[, -1])
rownames(mash_matrix) <- row_names
colnames(mash_matrix) <- row_names
# Keep only those tree tip labels that are also present in the matrix
common_labels <- snp_tree_tip_order[snp_tree_tip_order %in% rownames(mash_matrix)]
# Reorder the matrix rows and columns accordingly
mash_matrix <- mash_matrix[common_labels, common_labels]
mash_matrix[upper.tri(mash_matrix)] <- NA

#----- PANGENOME WRANGLING ------# 

# Read and manipulate gene presence-absence data (Panaroo)
pangenome_tab <- fread(pan_rtab)
pangenome_roary <- fread(pan_roary) %>%
  select(Gene, Annotation,`Genome Fragment`)

pangenome <- pangenome_tab %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Gene, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(tempvar = "Gene-presence absence",
         Gene = factor(Gene, levels = pangenome_tab$Gene),
         sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = snp_tree_tip_order)
         ) %>% 
  merge(pangenome_roary, by = "Gene") %>%
  mutate(hovertext = paste("Gene:", Gene, "<br>",
                            "Annotation:", Annotation, "<br>",
                            "Genome Fragment:", `Genome Fragment`,  "<br>"
                              ))

## Read and reorder Gene distance matrix (Panaroo)
genes_df <- fread(pan_genedists)
row_names <- genes_df[[1]]
genes_matrix <- as.matrix(genes_df[, -1])
rownames(genes_matrix) <- row_names
colnames(genes_matrix) <- row_names
genes_matrix <- genes_matrix[snp_tree_tip_order, snp_tree_tip_order]
genes_matrix[upper.tri(genes_matrix)] <- NA

## Read Pangenome statistics
panaroo_stats_text <- readLines(pan_summary)

# Ensure Pangenome statistics file ends with a newline character
if (length(panaroo_stats_text) > 0 && !grepl("\\n$", panaroo_stats_text[length(panaroo_stats_text)])) {
    writeLines(c(panaroo_stats_text, ""), pan_summary)
}

# Custom function
custom_plot_function <- function(plot) {
  if (length(samples$sample_id) > 35) {
    size <- length(samples$sample_id) * 20
    ggplotly(plot, tooltip = "text", height = size, width = size)
  } else if (length(samples$sample_id) > 20) {
    size <- length(samples$sample_id) * 20
    ggplotly(plot, tooltip = "text", height = size)
  } else {
    ggplotly(plot, tooltip = "text")
  }
}

```

## Disclaimer

***This report is only for investigation and epidemiology use. It should NOT be used for diagnosis, treatment, or management of patients and should NOT be included in any patient health record.***

*The data presented in this report has not been validated or subjected to CLIA standards for diagnosing and treating disease. Methods outlined throughout the report are still in development and may be subject to change.*


## Genomic Assessment

Cluster analysis was performed on `r length(unique(samples$sample_id))` samples of the species *`r species`* in the cluster named **`r cluster_id`**. Core genome and pangenome profiles were compared between isolates.

### Core-SNP Tree

```{r snp-tree-plot}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache.vars = TRUE)

phylocanvas(
      snp_tree,
      treetype = "rectangular",
      showscalebar = TRUE)
```

***Figure 1.** Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree constructed from core single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) identified using Snippy-core. Tree inference was performed with IQ-TREE under the GTR+G4 substitution model. Branch lengths represent the average number of nucleotide substitutions per site across the core genome alignment with constant sites included, incorporating site-specific rate variation modeled by a gamma distribution. As horizontal gene transfer (HGT) and recombination can obscure vertical inheritance, branch lengths should be interpreted with caution. Very short or near-zero branches indicate unresolved relationships, often due to highly similar or identical samples. Such regions of the tree should be interpreted with caution, and complementary analyses (e.g., SNP distance matrices) may be needed to clarify fine-scale linkages. The reference genome was excluded, and the tree was midpoint-rooted. Visualization was generated using Phylocanvas.*

### Recombination filtered SNP Tree

```{r gubbins-tree-plot}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache.vars = TRUE)

phylocanvas(
      gub_tree,
      treetype = "rectangular",
      showscalebar = TRUE)
```
***Figure 2.** Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree based on recombination-filtered core single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), inferred using Gubbins and constructed with IQ-TREE under the GTR+G4 substitution model. The alignment includes both variable and invariant sites, allowing branch lengths to represent the average number of nucleotide substitutions per site across the core genome alignment. Very short or near-zero branches indicate unresolved relationships, often due to highly similar or identical samples. Such regions of the tree should be interpreted with caution, and complementary analyses (e.g., SNP distance matrices) may be needed to clarify fine-scale linkages. The reference genome was excluded, and the tree is midpoint-rooted. Visualization was generated using Phylocanvas.*


### Mash Tree

```{r mash-tree-plot}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache.vars = TRUE)

phylocanvas(
      mash_tree,
      treetype = "rectangular",
      showscalebar = TRUE)
```

***Figure 3.**Tree constructed using MashTree based on pairwise genomic distances estimated by the MinHash algorithm (Mash). Distances were used to generate a dendrogram via the neighbor-joining (NJ) algorithm implemented in QuickTree. This tree reflects overall genomic similarity and does not represent a true phylogeny. Only samples with available genome assemblies were included in the Mash analysis. The reference genome was excluded, and the tree is midpoint-rooted. Visualization was created using Phylocanvas.*

The Pangenome summary statistics for cluster `r cluster_id` are as follows:

```{r panaroo-stats, echo=FALSE}

cat(panaroo_stats_text, sep="\n")
```

```{r pangenome-plot}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache.vars = TRUE)

#----- PANGENOME HEATMAP ------#
pangenome_plot <- ggplot(pangenome, aes(y = sample_id, x = Gene, fill = Value, text = hovertext)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_color_identity() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), 
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none"
        ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkblue")

custom_plot_function(pangenome_plot)
```

***Figure 4.** Gene presence–absence heatmap from a pangenome analysis performed with Panaroo. Blue indicates gene presence; white indicates absence. The x-axis represents individual genes, and the y-axis represents isolates. Sample order follows the core SNP-based phylogeny. Gene names and annotation can be interactively displayed when hovering the cursor over individual tiles. Visualization created using ggplot2 and plotly.*

### Core SNP distance matrix

```{r snp-matrix}

##---CORE SNP MATRIX---###

# Convert matrix to data frame
snp_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(snp_matrix)))
colnames(snp_df) <- c("sample_id_row", "sample_id_col", "value")
snp_df <- snp_df %>% 
  mutate(sample_id_row = factor(sample_id_row, levels = snp_tree_tip_order),
         sample_id_col = factor(sample_id_col, levels = snp_tree_tip_order),
         hovertext = paste0("Row: ", sample_id_row, "<br>",
                           "Col: ", sample_id_col, "<br>",
                           "SNPs: ", value, "<br>"
                           ))

# Filter the data to include only significant SNP values
snp_df_links <- snp_df %>%
filter(value <= 40)
    
# Create the heatmap
snps_heatmap_plot <- ggplot(snp_df, aes(x = sample_id_col, y = sample_id_row, fill = value, text = hovertext)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  geom_text(data = snp_df_links, aes(label = value), color = "black", size = 3, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#4E79A7", high = "white") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 8),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.title = element_blank()) +
  labs(fill = "SNPs")
  
# Convert to plotly object and add hover info from text by using tooltip
custom_plot_function(snps_heatmap_plot)
```

***Figure 5.** Heatmap of core SNP distances among isolates. Values are shown for 0-40 SNPs. SNP distances were determined using the core-SNP alignment generated by Snippy, subsequently analyzed using snp-dists. Specific SNP differences can be displayed upon hovering over the heatmap cells. Sample order follows the core SNP-based phylogeny. Visualization created using ggplot2 and plotly.*

## Methods

### SNP Analysis

Reference-based SNP analysis was accomplished using Snippy v4.6.0^1^ within a species-specific clusters. Phylogenetic trees were generated using IQTREE2 v2.4.0^2^ and pairwise SNP distances were calculated using snp-dists v0.8.2^3^.

### Pangenome Analysis

The gene presence-absence profile was identified using the pangenome tool Panaroo v1.5.2^4^ with a strict mode, using 95% sequence identity for clustering and a 70% protein family sequence identity threshold.

### Recombination Analysis

The identification and masking of loci containing elevated densities of base substitutions, which are marked as recombinations, was done with Gubbins v3.4.3^5^. Recombination-filtered SNPs were extracted with SNP-Sites v2.5.1^6^ followed by SNP-based phylogeny using IQTREE2 v2.4.0^2^.

### Mash Analysis

The determination of MinHash distances and Mash tree generation were done with MashTree v1.4.6^7^.
